source_text:
Sermo de obitu sanctorum trium puerorum
ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ ΑΡΧΙΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΥ ΑΛΕΞΑΝ∆ΡΕΙΑΣ ΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ
ΤΕΛΕΥΤΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΓΙΩΝ ΤΡΙΩΝ ΠΑΙ∆ΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΝΣΟΦΟΥ ∆ΑΝΙΗΛ.
Πρόφασις καιρῶν παρέστη, ἀγαπητοὶ, μαρτύρων ἀγαθῶν ἐνέγκαι μνήμην·
αὕτη γὰρ ἡ μνήμη μιμεῖται τὴν πανήγυριν τῶν οὐρανίων ταγμάτων, ἐπὶ πρεσβείαν
καὶ σωτηρίαν τῶν ἡμετέρων ψυχῶν· ὅσοι οὖν τὸν Θεὸν ἐπιγινώσκετε, σήμερον
ἐνταῦθα τὰς ἀκοὰς ὑμῶν προτείνατε, ὅπως ἀξιωθῆτε τοῦ βραβείου τῶν ἀρτίως
λεγομένων μαρτύρων· τούτους γὰρ ἐπαινεῖσθαι καὶ θαυμάζειν χρὴ τοὺς μήπω
θεασαμένους ἐνανθρώπησιν Χριστοῦ, καὶ θάνατον ἀθανάτου, καὶ ἀνάστασιν ἐκ
νεκρῶν, καὶ πρὸ τῆς ἐνσάρκου παρουσίας, ὁμολογητὰς καὶ μάρτυρας αὐτοῦ
thought_title: A timely remembrance of the martyrs
orientation: Cyril, archbishop of Alexandria, opens a sermon to the congregation on the death of the holy three young men and the all-wise Daniel, urging them to honor the martyrs.
pass_a_gloss: A pretext of seasons has presented itself, beloved, to bring remembrance of good martyrs; for this remembrance imitates the celebration of the heavenly orders, for intercession and salvation of our souls; as many of you therefore as know God, today stretch out your ears here, so that you may be deemed worthy of the prize of the martyrs just now being spoken of; for it is necessary to praise and marvel at these who have not yet seen the incarnation of Christ, and the death of the immortal one, and the resurrection from the dead, and who before the incarnation were martyrs and confessors of him.

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of πρόφασις as occasion or pretext, and καιρῶν as seasons or times, without smoothing into idiomatic English.
Literal rendering of the infinitive phrase; preserves the action of bringing memory.
Literal rendering of the idiom for attentive listening; keeps the physical metaphor.

choices.english: be deemed worthy of the prize
choices.why: Preserves the passive of ἀξιόω with genitive, and the glossary term βραβεῖον as prize.
rejected: be counted worthy of the award

choices.why: Uses the glossary English for ἐνανθρώπησις.
Uses the glossary English for ἔνσαρκος παρουσία.

pass_b_english: Beloved, a timely occasion has arisen to bring remembrance of good martyrs. This remembrance imitates the celebration of the heavenly orders, for the intercession and salvation of our souls. So all of you who know God, stretch out your ears here today, so that you may be deemed worthy of the prize of the martyrs now being spoken of. For these are the ones we must praise and marvel at: they had not yet seen the incarnation of Christ, nor the death of the Immortal One, nor the resurrection from the dead, and yet even before the bodily coming they were his confessors and martyrs.

problems.quote: nor the death of the immortal one
problems.why: Source means 'death of the Immortal One' (Christ); lowercase 'immortal one' obscures the Christological reference.
problems.fix: nor the death of the Immortal One
problems.ruling: ἀθανάτου is articular/qualitative: 'the Immortal One' = Christ; lowercase obscures Christological title.

edits.old: nor the death of the immortal one
edits.new: nor the death of the Immortal One

problems.why: Same concept reversed; reader may miss identity.
problems.fix: Keep consistent order or note equivalence.

problems.why: Two terms for same theological concept; reader may think distinct.
problems.fix: Use one term or gloss as equivalent.

problems.why: Same Greek concept? Reader may not connect advocacy with intercession.
problems.fix: Unify or note 'advocacy' means intercessory role.

edits.old: and yet even before the bodily coming they were his confessors and martyrs.
edits.new: and yet even before the bodily coming they were his martyrs and confessors.

fixed: The English already says 'incarnation' and 'bodily coming' as distinct terms matching the source's distinct terms; no change needed.
The English already says 'intercession' matching the source's 'πρεσβείαν'; no change needed.

problems.why: Same Greek term rendered two ways; reader may miss they are identical.

edits.old: and yet even before the bodily coming they were his martyrs and confessors.
edits.new: and yet even before the incarnation they were his martyrs and confessors.

fixed: Standardized 'bodily coming' to 'incarnation' in both the English and the literal gloss to match the glossary term and avoid the reader missing that the same Greek term is rendered two ways.
